name: apple-hig
description: Use when designing, implementing, or reviewing interfaces for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, CarPlay, or other Apple system experiences using Apple's Human Interface Guidelines. Routes to current platform, foundation, pattern, component, input, and technology guidance.
license: MIT
metadata:
  author: AyushRajSinghParihar
  source: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines

# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
   For platform support, product feasibility, or platform adaptation, first read each relevant
   platform's Getting started procedure, then the specific component or technology
   procedure. Check both the platform model and the surface's support limits.
3. Before finalizing the route, search the [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md)
   for the task's concepts as well as component or framework names. Its trigger
   descriptions connect everyday product requests to Apple's topic names; users
   need not name an Apple framework. Read the owning family and matching topic
   procedure before its supporting reference. Search relevant rows instead of
   loading the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Map the brief's material decisions to their owning topics. Read the owning
   procedure for each explicit concern, such as privacy or accessibility, as well
   as the affected components; a neighboring procedure's reminder is insufficient.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.
   In a review, map each supplied control to its candidate component procedure
   even when markup or behavior is missing. Use it to frame inspection questions;
   missing evidence neither proves a defect nor removes that control from scope.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Task | Read this topic skill |
|---|---|
| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |
| Onboarding, loading, search, sharing, accounts, feedback, media, settings | [Patterns](subskills/apple-hig-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Charts, images, text views, embedded web content | [Content](subskills/apple-hig-content/SKILL.md) |
| Lists, collections, split views, tab views, disclosure and grouping | [Layout and organization](subskills/apple-hig-layout-and-organization/SKILL.md) |
| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

# Apple HIG: Translate information hierarchy into containers

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Map records, groups, selection and supporting detail before choosing lists, collections, split views, tabs or disclosure. Open the procedure for the candidate container.
2. Separate grouping from navigation: a box organizes related content; a split view coordinates hierarchical panes; disclosure reveals optional detail. Do not use a container merely because space is available.
3. For resizing, large content and empty states, retain a coherent selection and route back. Identify minimum useful pane/content behavior from the task rather than fixed screenshots.
4. Deliver the hierarchy, selection model, adaptive layout decisions and a patch or verification matrix covering narrow and expanded states.

## Enter the topic procedure

Read the selected topic’s SKILL.md before its supporting guidance. For a review,
inspect actual evidence and return findings; for an implementation request, make
the authorized change; for design or adaptation, produce a usable specification
or patch. Load related topics only when the chosen procedure calls for them.

name: apple-hig-boxes
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting bordered groups of related controls or information.

# Give each boundary a reason

Read [the box guide](../../references/boxes.md). This procedure is application advice; platform conventions come from the guide.

Inspect the screen/code, target platform, requested create/review/adapt mode, and relationships among enclosed items. Identify whether a boundary communicates a real group, or merely decorates the whole screen. Record available width, titles, and nested boundaries; do not infer accessibility grouping from a screenshot.

First express subgroups with alignment and spacing. Retain a box when its boundary makes a meaningful group easier to understand; keep it smaller than its container so surrounding context remains visible. Add a brief sentence-case title when the relationship needs explanation or an accessible introduction. Apply the settings-pane colon exception only in that context. On iOS/iPadOS use appropriate semantic background treatment; on Mac account for the title above the box. Do not propose the component on tvOS/watchOS, where the guide marks it unsupported; adapt the relationship through suitable layout.

Implement the requested grouping, supply a concrete annotated layout, or report specific redundant/misleading boundaries in review. Preserve control relationships and reading order when removing a border.

**Worked transformation:** Before: printer settings have one screen-sized border and three nested borders around paper options. Decision: the outer edge adds no relationship; paper size and orientation already group through alignment. After: remove the outer border, use spacing for subgroups, and retain a titled `Paper options:` group only where it helps explain the controls.

Deliver the changed layout and group/title rationale. Verify narrow layouts, larger text, and that the title introduces the intended controls in the accessibility structure. Fail for cramped nested boundaries, a title attached to the wrong group, or a box that obscures context. Separate source inspection from native assistive execution.

Load [labels](../apple-hig-labels/SKILL.md) for title semantics or [layout](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-layout/SKILL.md) when spacing is the underlying issue.

name: apple-hig-labels
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting short uneditable text and its relationship to nearby controls.

# Make short text carry the right context

Read [the labels guide](../../references/labels.md). Apply its documented semantics; the procedure is application advice.

Inspect text, surrounding controls, platform, and create/review/adapt intent. Determine whether each string is a static caption, editable value, long-form content, or useful portable information. Record its association, hierarchy, truncation, scaling, and copy behavior where evidenced.

Choose a field for short editing and a text view for longer/formatted content. Keep labels actual text with system typography and semantic colors appropriate to primary/supporting/unavailable meaning. Do not assign a faint semantic role solely to make essential content visually quiet. Preserve Dynamic Type where supported and inspect custom-font readability. Allow copying when an error, location, or address needs reuse. On watchOS, use system date/time or timer text for temporal values rather than repeatedly rebuilding a static label; do not imply every framework provides Apple's automatic updating behavior.

Implement the label and association, provide concrete replacement text/style rules, or review identifiable ambiguity/legibility issues. Apply component-specific wording conventions when the label belongs to a button or another constrained control.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a shipping screen shows `ID` in faint gray above an uncopyable tracking number rendered as an image. Decision: the identifier is primary portable information, not unavailable content. After: label it `Tracking Number`, render the value as scalable selectable text, and reserve secondary hierarchy for supporting delivery notes.

Deliver the edited text and semantic/association contract. Verify long localization, enlarged/bold text, appearance changes, copy where relevant, and accessible association with the correct control. Fail for a label attached to the wrong input, rasterized essential text, or loss of meaning through clipping. Report native text/assistive rendering separately from code inspection.

Load [text-views](../../../apple-hig-content/.topics/apple-hig-text-views/SKILL.md) for longer selectable material or [text-fields](../../../apple-hig-selection-and-input/.topics/apple-hig-text-fields/SKILL.md) when the value is editable.

# Apple HIG: End-to-end behavior and recovery

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Trace the person’s task from entry through completion, cancellation, interruption and recovery. Select the pattern procedure for the actual failure or desired behavior before selecting its controls.
2. Preserve the current work, selection and navigation context across the transitions that matter. Choose interruption or modality according to urgency and task scope, not visual emphasis.
3. For asynchronous or recurring work, separate current progress, eventual result, error recovery and unavailable capability. For audio/video/haptics, specify user control and environmental behavior.
4. Deliver a transition/state specification, a correction to the supplied flow, or ranked findings tied to observed steps. Test alternate exits and resumption, not just the success path.

name: apple-hig-settings
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting app-wide configuration, task-local options, system preferences, and settings access or persistence.
---

# Put an option where its effect is understood

Read [the settings guide](../../references/settings.md). This workflow is application advice; platform locations and system preference scope constrain the design.

Inspect option inventory/frequency, affected scope, defaults, system counterparts, platform, and create/review/adapt intent. Classify task-local, document-wide, app-wide, and system-wide choices. Record actual capability detection/persistence rather than treating a displayed toggle as proof.

Choose sensible defaults and detect capabilities instead of asking for information already known. Keep frequent view/task options beside their visible effect and rare app-wide choices in settings. Do not duplicate system accessibility/authentication/scrolling preferences with misleading scope. Reserve system Settings entries for rare changes. On Mac place app Settings in the app menu with expected access, document setup in File, and use stable settings-pane navigation/title/restoration rather than a customizable main toolbar. Watch cannot add custom entries to system Settings; keep only essential in-app options. Preserve familiar game access where appropriate.

Implement option placement/persistence or provide a scope/default/location contract; reviews identify exact misplaced or contradictory settings. Do not expand a settings redesign into unauthorized global configuration changes.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a Mac map app puts its layer filter in app Settings and a global Reduce Motion copy in the main toolbar, while document scale changes every map. Decision: frequency and scope are inverted. After: keep layers local, respect system motion preference, and separate document scale from app-wide defaults.

Deliver the artifact, option scope, defaults/detection, access, and restoration policy. Verify default/changed values, reopen/last pane, per-document independence, and capability changes. Fail for misleading global/local scope, duplicated conflicting system preference, or lost expected settings access. Native settings/shortcut behavior requires execution evidence.

Load [the-menu-bar](../../../apple-hig-menus-and-actions/.topics/apple-hig-the-menu-bar/SKILL.md), [toggles](../../../apple-hig-selection-and-input/.topics/apple-hig-toggles/SKILL.md), or [onboarding](../apple-hig-onboarding/SKILL.md) for access, state controls, or deferred setup.

# Apple HIG: Perception, meaning and adaptable presentation

requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify the actual barrier or design decision: readability, visual hierarchy, imagery meaning, movement, locale, privacy or spatial placement. Choose the corresponding topic procedure rather than loading every foundation.
2. For text access, combine Typography with Accessibility only where size, reflow or reading alternatives matter. Use VoiceOver when grouping, semantics or navigation needs a procedure of its own.
3. For color/material decisions, separate content hierarchy from controls and evaluate the actual appearance/background/settings context. Preserve semantic meaning when appearance changes.
4. Deliver prioritized evidence-backed corrections or a concrete presentation specification. Distinguish inspected contrast/layout evidence from runtime and assistive-technology checks still needed.

# Preserve relationships while available space changes

Read [Layout](../../references/layout.md). Inspect content priority, navigation, controls, supported environments, constraints, and current implementation. Identify design/review/adaptation mode and keep the existing layout system. Record actual available space and text/localization conditions; device names alone are insufficient evidence for a breakpoint.

Start with relationships: align peers, group related items, indent subordinates, and reveal secondary choices progressively. Place important content toward the leading/top region in the locale's reading order. Separate backgrounds that can extend beneath bars from important content/actions that must respect safe regions.

Choose adaptations from available width/height and environmental values, not a phone/tablet or portrait/landscape guess. Preserve selection, content, functionality, and idiom when columns collapse, actions overflow, or horizontal rows stack for larger text. Test the smallest and largest useful layouts first, then intermediate resizing, longer localization, direction changes, and display accommodations. Crop decorative backgrounds without distorting aspect ratio or hiding essential imagery.

Apply platform conditions deliberately: Mac essential controls cannot depend on a bottom edge that may be offscreen; TV content needs the guide's overscan insets and focus-expansion room; Watch normally needs very few side-by-side actions. visionOS windows/volumes should resize, use meaningful bounds, and avoid inline 3D crowding controls; use separate volumes for model-centric work. Read numeric platform specifications from the guide rather than generalizing one platform's spacing.

**Before → decision → after:** A reading list positions Delete at a fixed bottom coordinate and fixes each row to one line. Decision: resized windows and enlarged titles need flow-based layout. After, row height/wrapping adapt, secondary actions remain reachable through contextual overflow, and the selected article persists when the sidebar collapses.

Deliver corrected layouts/constraints or implementation plus an environment matrix. Fail if a required action disappears, related items detach, content overlaps hardware/bars, or resizing changes the task's meaning. Report tested dimensions/settings; static or Linux checks cannot establish native safe-area/focus behavior absent supported execution.

Use [Typography](../apple-hig-typography/SKILL.md) for text behavior, [Right to left](../apple-hig-right-to-left/SKILL.md) for direction, and [Spatial layout](../apple-hig-spatial-layout/SKILL.md) for 3D position/scale.

# Boxes Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/boxes) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. A box visually groups related information and controls with a border or contrasting background; a title can explain the relationship. ## Best practices Keep a box meaningfully smaller than its containing window or screen so the boundary communicates a group without crowding surrounding content. For subgroups, use alignment and spacing before adding nested borders; nested boxes can make the interface feel cramped. ## Content Add a short introductory title when the relationship is not obvious or when it helps VoiceOver users anticipate the contents. Use a brief sentence-case phrase. Omit terminal punctuation except for a box title in a settings pane, which takes a colon. ## Platform considerations visionOS has no additional guidance. Boxes are unsupported in tvOS and watchOS. ### iOS, iPadOS System boxes normally use secondary and tertiary background colors. ### macOS The default placement puts the title above the box. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Layout](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/layout) #### Developer documentation — SwiftUI — AppKit

# Labels Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/labels) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. A label presents short, uneditable text, including an action name, list-item description, or context for nearby controls. SwiftUI provides both Text and Label; component-specific guidance may further constrain the wording. ## Best practices Use a text field for a short editable value and a text view for longer or richly formatted content. Prefer system typography and retain Dynamic Type support where available; check readability whenever introducing custom fonts or styling. Permit selection and copying when the text conveys useful portable information such as an error, address, or location. Use semantic label colors to express hierarchy rather than hard-coded tones: | Role | Typical use | UIKit name | AppKit name | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Primary | Main information | label | labelColor | | Secondary | Supporting text or subheading | secondaryLabel | secondaryLabelColor | | Tertiary | Description of unavailable behavior | tertiaryLabel | tertiaryLabelColor | | Quaternary | Watermark | quaternaryLabel | quaternaryLabelColor | The UIKit column applies to iOS, iPadOS, tvOS, and visionOS. ## Platform considerations No additional iOS, iPadOS, tvOS, or visionOS rules are specified. ### macOS An NSTextField configured as noneditable can display label text. ### watchOS Use system date/time and timer text components for changing temporal information. Date text supports formats, calendars, and time zones; timer text supports count-up and countdown formats. The system adapts presentation to available space and updates values without further app work. These components are also useful in complications. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Text fields](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/text-fields) [Text views](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/text-views) #### Developer documentation — SwiftUI — SwiftUI — UIKit — AppKit ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: June 5, 2023.

# Layout Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/layout) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Use predictable relationships among content and controls while adapting to the actual available space. ## Visual hierarchy Prioritize important content toward the top and leading edge in reading order. Use system components for RTL adaptation. Align related items, indent subordinate items, and group relationships with space, containers, or separators. Reveal secondary choices progressively through disclosure, menus, nested views, or scrollable media sections. Distinguish navigation/controls with Liquid Glass and scroll-edge treatments; extend full-window backgrounds under bars and sidebars. A background extension effect can mirror and blur imagery under adjacent components instead of hiding essential original art. ## Adaptability Handle size classes, display sizes, orientation/aspect ratio, Dynamic Island, external displays, Display Zoom, resizable windows, text changes, localized length/direction/fonts, and date/number formats. Use SwiftUI or Auto Layout, safe areas, margins, and layout modifiers. Orientation-locked games must still resize. With large text, stack horizontal content, increase row height, and allow wrapping. Apple’s Unity accessibility plug-in can supply Dynamic Type in games. Preview smallest/largest layouts first, then multiple devices, localizations, sizes, iPad resizing, and iPhone Mirroring. Scale backgrounds to fill without distorting aspect ratio; extreme wide/short or narrow/tall windows may crop much more than standard displays. ### Size classes Each axis is compact or regular, describing available width or height rather than device type or orientation. All four combinations can occur as apps resize, multitask, or mirror. Base layout on these environmental values, not idiom/orientation guesses. Preserve functionality across classes while changing how much is exposed, such as sidebar versus tabs or visible actions versus overflow. The platform idiom remains the same during resizing, so preserve its familiar character. ## Guides and safe areas Layout guides supply rectangular regions for alignment, spacing, margins, and readable text widths; custom guides can add app-specific structure. Safe areas exclude edge obstructions such as camera hardware, status bars, tab bars, and toolbars. Keep important content and controls within the appropriate safe regions. ## Platform considerations No extra iOS/iPadOS rules are listed. ### macOS Do not rely on the bottom of a window for essential controls because it may sit below the physical display. Avoid placing content behind the top camera housing. ### tvOS Inset primary content 60 pt vertically and 80 pt horizontally to withstand TV overscan/settings. Leave enough focus padding for system enlargement so focused items do not obscure important information. #### Grids Use consistent row/column spacing, sufficient room for enlargement, and symmetrical partial items at both horizontal edges. Add extra separation above and below row titles. UIKit collection flow layout derives the column count from item width and spacing. Source grid measurements follow; all use 40 pt horizontal gaps and a minimum 100 pt vertical gap between unfocused rows. #### Two-column grid Unfocused item width: 860 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Three-column grid Unfocused item width: 560 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Four-column grid Unfocused item width: 410 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Five-column grid Unfocused item width: 320 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Six-column grid Unfocused item width: 260 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Seven-column grid Unfocused item width: 217 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Eight-column grid Unfocused item width: 184 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Nine-column grid Unfocused item width: 160 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. ### visionOS Support resizing in windows and volumes; center content horizontally at very large sizes. Set minimum/maximum bounds only to avoid overlaps or unwieldy layouts, not to disable resizing. Use inline 3D content sparingly for meaningful additions; inset it so it avoids controls and window edges. Prefer volumes or immersive spaces for large/model-centric content. Open supplemental content in an adjacent window, reserving ornaments for interactive app controls. Space controls so hover feedback remains distinct; regular buttons should have centers at least 60 pt apart. ### watchOS Normally use no more than three glyph buttons or two text buttons side by side. Full-width text controls usually work best; two short labels can fit on a non-scrolling screen. Support autorotation when people may show content, such as a photo or QR code, to another person or reader instead of always sleeping on wrist-away movement. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/layout) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: September 9, 2026, September 9, 2025, June 9, 2025, March 7, 2025, September 9, 2024, June 10, 2024, February 2, 2024, December 5, 2023, September 15, 2023, June 21, 2023, September 14, 2022.

# Settings Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/settings) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Use sensible defaults and respect system preferences. App-wide configuration, task-local controls, and system Settings belong in different places according to how often and where people need them. ## Best practices Optimize defaults for most people and automatically detect capabilities such as connected controllers or appearance. Keep the settings set small. Support expected access, including Command-Comma and game Escape. Do not duplicate systemwide accessibility, scrolling, or authentication settings in a way that suggests they have different scope. ## General settings Put infrequently changed experience-wide choices, such as window configuration, saving behavior, key mappings, or account preferences, in the app's settings area. ## Task-specific options Expose frequent view/task changes where their effects are visible: filtering, reordering, and showing/hiding content. In games, approach to a current challenge normally belongs to gameplay rather than a settings trip. ## System settings Reserve system-app entries for the rarest changes and, where useful, link directly from the app. ## Platform considerations No additional iOS, iPadOS, tvOS, or visionOS rules are specified. ### macOS Place Settings in the app menu, not the main toolbar; document-level configuration belongs in File. A settings window can use a stable noncustomizable always-visible pane toolbar with active selection. Dim minimize/zoom because reopening is easy and size follows the pane. Use the current pane as title, or App Name Settings for one pane, and restore the previously visited pane. ### watchOS Apps do not add custom entries to system Settings. Offer only essential options, perhaps at the main view's bottom or through More for object configuration. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Onboarding](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/onboarding) #### Developer documentation — SwiftUI — Foundation ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: June 10, 2024.

# Expose the task's structure without relying on sight

Read [VoiceOver](../../references/voiceover.md). Inspect the task, actual accessibility semantics when available, visible content, dynamic updates, and requested design/review/adaptation. Preserve the existing stack. A screenshot cannot establish spoken names, rotor behavior, focus order, or successful nonvisual operation; distinguish proposals from inspected runtime semantics.

Name important controls by actual function, improve unhelpful generic labels, and synchronize descriptions/values with changing content. Describe meaningful imagery only for information the image conveys beyond nearby captions; hide decoration from navigation. For charts, expose a concise purpose plus accessible equivalents for every interaction, not merely a label saying “Chart.”

Build navigation structure from the task. Give pages short unique titles and meaningful section headings. Express grouping, links, ordering, and relationships otherwise conveyed by proximity/alignment, following locale reading order and grouping captions with their own images. Mark headings/links for rotor navigation and notify assistive technologies of relevant content/layout changes without inventing untested announcement behavior.

On visionOS, custom-gesture apps do not normally receive hand input while VoiceOver exploration is active. Direct Gesture mode changes that relationship and disables standard VoiceOver gestures; provide an alternative task route instead of requiring every person to switch modes or depend on custom hands.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a sales chart exposes one unlabeled canvas and decorative stars interrupt the reading sequence, while changing a date updates only the visual title. Decision: nonvisual readers need structure, current values, and equivalent chart actions. After, a named section describes the chart's purpose, date controls expose current values, accessible summaries/actions cover comparisons, decorations leave navigation, and relevant updates are represented through supported semantics.

Deliver a semantic name/role/value/group/order specification or implementation with a nonvisual task walkthrough. Fail if a necessary action is unnamed/unreachable, values become stale, captions detach, or chart interaction has no equivalent. Report actual VoiceOver/rotor/device tests separately; Linux/static checks cannot claim screen-reader execution.

Use [Accessibility](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-accessibility/SKILL.md) for broader sensory/input barriers, [Writing](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-writing/SKILL.md) for descriptions, or [Gestures](../../../apple-hig-inputs/.topics/apple-hig-gestures/SKILL.md) for spatial alternatives.

# VoiceOver Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/voiceover) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. VoiceOver makes interface and content usable without visual access, including Apple-platform games and Unity experiences using Apple’s plug-ins. ## Descriptions Label every important element, improving generic system labels to describe actual function and labeling custom controls. Keep descriptions synchronized with changing content. Describe meaningful images only for information they themselves convey, avoiding redundant surrounding captions. Give charts/infographics a concise purpose description and accessible equivalents of every interaction. Hide purely decorative imagery from accessibility navigation to reduce irrelevant speech. ## Navigation Give each page a short unique title and meaningful section headings. Express grouping, order, links, and relationships otherwise conveyed only through proximity/alignment. Use the current locale’s reading sequence and group images with their own captions. Notify assistive technologies when visible content or layout changes. Identify headings, links, and other content for rotor navigation; the rotor can also offer braille keyboard access. ## Platform considerations No extra iOS/iPadOS/macOS/tvOS/watchOS rules are listed. ### visionOS With VoiceOver enabled, custom-gesture apps do not receive hand input by default, preventing accidental app actions during accessible exploration. A person may enable Direct Gesture mode, which turns off standard VoiceOver gestures and lets the app receive hand input directly. Application advice: do not make custom gestures the only route through the experience. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/voiceover) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: March 7, 2025.

# Revised Mac scanner settings interaction specification

## Basis and decisions

"'`interface.md` supplies a text description: resolution, file destination and unrelated account deletion share six heavy nested outlined boxes; “Advanced” appears three times; the window can become narrow. It supplies no screenshot, implementation, option inventory, dimensions, or persistence behavior. The exact nesting and control types are unknown.

Use a single column of two unboxed semantic groups, in this order:

| Group heading | Contents | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Scan quality | Resolution, with its current value and existing editing control | Describes the scan property being changed. |
| Save location | File destination, with its current value and existing editing control | Describes where output goes. |

Remove all six outlined containers and all three generic “Advanced” labels. Use alignment and space to establish relationships; add no replacement outer border. This is a design choice applying Apple'"'s preference for spacing/alignment before nested borders, rather than a rule that boxes are forbidden. With only two known settings, neither disclosure nor tabs improve the task. Keep both settings visible. [Boxes — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/boxes#Best-practices).

Use plain section headings “Scan quality” and “Save location”, without punctuation. These are unboxed headings. If a later, evidenced inventory justifies a box, its short sentence-case settings-pane title takes a colon and sits above the box on Mac; do not apply that exception to every heading. [Boxes — Content and macOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/boxes#Content).

Move the existing account deletion action to the app's Account settings pane, outside the scanner panel. If no Account pane exists, add an Account destination in the app's settings navigation and put the action there. Navigating there must not trigger deletion. Retain its existing action flow; deletion confirmation, authentication and recovery behavior are not evidenced or redesigned here. This placement is a product decision grounded in the distinction between account preferences and task settings. [Settings — General settings](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/settings#General-settings).

## Scope, state and transitions

For this specification, treat this panel as app-wide **scanner defaults**, not as edits to an already running scan. That scope is a proposed product contract, not an observation. Title the pane “Scanner”; add supporting text “Defaults for new scans.” If the actual product uses current-job options, keep these groups beside the scan workflow and change that scope text before implementation; do not silently change existing setting scope. Apple recommends keeping frequent task options near their effects. [Settings — Task-specific options](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/settings#Task-specific-options).

Retain the existing supported resolution choices, destination editor, validation and commit policy. The brief gives no basis for choosing a resolution value, inventing a folder, replacing controls, or converting Apply/Cancel to automatic saving. Existing stored values win on migration; for first use, retain the product's existing valid defaults. Detect scanner capabilities through the existing capability source rather than inventing choices. If capability detection or commit semantics do not exist, that integration contract remains unresolved before implementation.

Framework-agnostic structure and transition contract:

"'```text
ScannerPane(title="Scanner")
  supportingText("Defaults for new scans.")
  Group(id="quality", heading="Scan quality", border=none)
    Setting(id=existingResolutionID, label="Resolution",
            editor=existingResolutionEditor, value=existingResolutionValue)
  Group(id="save", heading="Save location", border=none)
    Setting(id=existingDestinationID, label="File destination",
            editor=existingDestinationEditor, value=existingDestinationValue)

open Scanner:
  bind existing settings model; restore existing values/pending edits as applicable
edit either setting:
  delegate to existing validation and commit flow; do not mutate the other setting
resize:
  recompute layout only; retain values, pending edits, focus and scroll context
leave for Account / close / reopen:
  use existing commit-or-cancel policy; do not silently discard pending edits
  restore previously visited settings pane under the app'"'s navigation policy
open Account:
  show existing account deletion action; opening the pane has no destructive effect
"'```

Keep app Settings access in the app menu with expected Command-Comma access; the scanner redesign must not remove existing access. Stable pane navigation should identify the selected pane and restore the last visited pane. These are requirements for integration, not claims about the supplied app. [Settings — macOS and Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/settings#macOS).

## Layout and semantic contract

Use these initial design tokens in logical layout units: 20 outer inset, 24 between groups, 8 between a heading and its content, and 12 between a field label and its editor. These are proposed tokens, not Apple-mandated measurements. Keep groups aligned to the same leading edge. Do not make “Resolution” or “File destination” faint to reduce visual weight.

At widths where the full label, gap and usable existing editor fit, place label and editor on one row. Otherwise stack label above editor with an 8-unit gap. Compute fit from actual localized text and editor minimum usable size, not a device name or an arbitrary fixed breakpoint. Stack destination editing actions as needed. Permit variable row heights and wrapping; keep the destination value selectable/copyable so a long location remains usable. Render labels as text with system-equivalent typography and semantic foreground roles. [Labels — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/labels#Best-practices).

Keep a vertical scrolling content region when height is insufficient. Do not pin required controls to an unreachable bottom edge or introduce horizontal scrolling for this form. Set a minimum supported window width only if an existing editor cannot remain operable after stacking; determine that limit by measurement during implementation. A resize must not hide a group, change its scope, reset a value, or collapse it. Apple calls for adaptation to available space and cautions against relying on the Mac window'"'s bottom edge for essential controls. [Layout — Adaptability and macOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/layout#Adaptability).

Expose named semantic groups introduced by their headings, and associate each field label with its own editor. Preserve the existing editor role and expose its current value, including updates. Logical reading order: pane title, scope description, Scan quality heading, Resolution editor, Save location heading, File destination editor and its associated actions. Keyboard traversal follows interactive elements in that order; headings are not extra Tab stops. Preserve the focused control's identity through reflow. Do not merge a group into a single inaccessible element that hides its editor. These are proposed semantics requiring runtime verification. [VoiceOver — Descriptions and Navigation](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/voiceover#Navigation).

## Worked before/after

**Before, as reported:** the user seeking resolution must interpret six heavy nested boxes and repeated “Advanced” labels; account deletion sits among scan settings. The brief does not establish exact control order or the number of clicks.

**After, illustrative values only:** a user opens Scanner, changes a supported resolution from 300 dpi to 600 dpi, then checks that the file destination remains "'`/Users/lee/Scans`. These values demonstrate independence; they are not new defaults or claims about hardware support.

```text
Wide                                     Narrow
Scanner                                  Scanner
Defaults for new scans.                  Defaults for new scans.

Scan quality                             Scan quality
Resolution       [600 dpi]               Resolution
                                         [600 dpi]
Save location
File destination [ /Users/lee/Scans ]     Save location
                                         File destination
                                         [ /Users/lee/Scans ]
```

Both layouts expose the same two groups without borders or “Advanced” disclosures. Resizing during editing leaves 600 dpi and the destination intact. The user reaches account deletion separately through Settings → Account. A nonvisual walkthrough follows the two named groups, hears each editor'"'s current value, edits resolution, then reaches the unchanged destination without encountering deletion.

## Acceptance checks and status

**Passed — document inspection only:** the supplied inventory is mapped: resolution → Scan quality, destination → Save location, deletion → Account. The revised structure has zero nested borders, zero repeated “Advanced” labels and explicit wide/narrow behavior. The specification defines state preservation and semantic associations. These passes concern this document, not an application.

**Failed — supplied design against this specification:** the described six nested outlined boxes, repeated generic labels and unrelated deletion action do not meet the revised grouping contract. Their presence is supported only by "'`interface.md`; no visual severity or runtime failure was measured.

**Not executed — implementation acceptance matrix:**

| Check | Observable pass criterion |
| --- | --- |
| Wide, narrow and intermediate resize | Both groups remain reachable; rows stack at measured fit limits; no clipping, overlap or horizontal scrolling. Record actual dimensions. |
| Short window | All editors and existing commit actions are reachable by scrolling and keyboard, without reliance on a fixed bottom edge. |
| Enlarged text and long localized strings | Headings stay with their groups; labels and values remain readable; actions remain operable. Record text settings and strings. |
| Values and reopening | Existing stored values survive migration; editing one field does not change the other; reopen/leave follows the existing commit policy. Test default and changed values. |
| Scanner changes | Existing capability handling yields valid choices or explains unavailable editing; no invented resolution or silent invalid substitution. |
| Account relocation | Deletion is absent from Scanner, reachable in Account, and never invoked by navigation; pending scanner edits follow the existing policy. |
| Keyboard and VoiceOver on Mac | Both editors are reachable, correctly named and valued in group order; reflow retains focus; no obsolete container or duplicate heading announcements. |
| Appearance and destination text | Light/dark appearance preserves readability; long destination values can be selected/copied without losing access to editing actions. |

## Evidence limits and audit trail

Used only `interface.md` and the installed package rooted at `.agents/skills/apple-hig/`. Explicitly read the root `SKILL.md`, searched relevant topic-index rows, then read each owning family and topic procedure before its supporting source guide: Layout and organization → Boxes and Labels; Patterns → Settings; Foundations → Layout; Technologies → VoiceOver. Each consumed file was read in its own shell command. Official URLs above identify the local guides'"' sources; they were not opened online.

The installed articles identify a 2026-10-25 snapshot/retrieval date. They are local application guidance, not SDK documentation or independent proof of current Apple behavior. The local settings guide describes pane-oriented sizing, while the brief explicitly requires narrow resizing; this specification preserves resizing and stable navigation, without imposing fixed pane dimensions.

No app code, screenshots, complete control inventory, device, SDK, GUI, scanner, keyboard interaction, or accessibility runtime was supplied or executed. No compilation, rendering, contrast measurement, VoiceOver result, actual supported resolution, commit behavior, or working Account pane is claimed.
